# `silk/bench/lines`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Benchmark result lines: the text format of Go's `testing` package, read and written.

## When to use
Use [`Lines.parse`](#Lines.impl.parse) to read the samples a benchmark program printed, in any language, and
[`Lines.fromResult`](#Lines.impl.fromResult) to hand a run to a tool that reads the format, such as `benchstat`. A
program that prints these lines needs no library: one `printf` per sample is enough.

## Details
A result line is one sample: a name, the number of iterations the sample covers, then one
or more pairs of a value and a unit. Values are for one iteration.

```text
impl: simdjson
BenchmarkParse/file=twitter 2000 165412 ns/op 1024 B/op
BenchmarkParse/file=twitter 2000 164980 ns/op 1024 B/op
```

A name starts with `Benchmark`, and the character after it is not a lowercase letter. A
configuration line is `key: value`, where the key starts with a lowercase letter and has no
space and no uppercase letter. It applies to every result line after it, until a line with
the same key replaces it. Every other line is ignored, so a program may print anything else.
Letters are judged as ASCII: a byte outside ASCII counts as lowercase.

A sample is never summarized by the program that prints it. It prints the line again for
the next sample, and `silk.bench.statistics` computes every statistic.

## Examples
```silk
import silk.bench.lines { Lines }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }

effect fn check() -> i32 ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let parsed = run Lines.parse("impl: silk\nBenchmarkParse 2000 165412 ns/op\nok 0.4s\n")
  let lines = parsed.lines.asSlice()
  if lines.length != 1 || lines[0].iterations != 2000 {
    return 1
  }
  return match Lines.value(&lines[0], "ns/op") {
    Option<f64>.Some { value } => if value == 165412.0 { 0 } else { 2 }
    Option<f64>.None => 3
  }
}

effect fn failed(error: OutOfMemoryError) -> i32 {
  drop error
  return 4
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run Effect.catchAll(check(), failed) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

<a id="Lines.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub effect fn parse(text: string) -> Parsed
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the result lines and configuration lines of `text`. A line that is neither is
ignored, and so is a line that starts like a result but has a part that does not parse,
such as a value that is not a number or a value with no unit.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the lines.

<a id="Lines.impl.setting"></a>

### Associated function `setting`

```silk
pub fn setting<'parsed>(parsed: &'parsed Parsed, at: usize, name: string) -> Option<
    string<'parsed>
  >
```

Returns the value of the configuration key `name` that applies to the result line at index
`at`: the last one written before that line. It is `None` when no line before it sets the
key.

<a id="Lines.impl.value"></a>

### Associated function `value`

```silk
pub fn value(line: &Line, unit: string) -> Option<f64>
```

Returns the value of `line` with the unit `unit`, or `None` when the line has none. When a
line repeats a unit, the first one is returned.

<a id="Lines.impl.named"></a>

### Associated function `named`

```silk
pub effect fn named(name: string) -> String
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the name a benchmark of a suite has as a result line: `Benchmark`, then `name` with
its first letter in uppercase and every space replaced by `_`. `parse/file=twitter` becomes
`BenchmarkParse/file=twitter`.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the text.

<a id="Lines.impl.fromResult"></a>

### Associated function `fromResult`

```silk
pub effect fn fromResult(result: &RunResult) -> String
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the samples of `result` as result lines, for a tool that reads the format.

Each implementation is a block that starts with the configuration line `impl: <name>` and,
when it has a revision, `revision:`, after the lines `suite:`, `date:` and, when the run
has one, `label:`. Each measured run
that succeeded is one line with 1 iteration and the units `ns/op` (time from start to
exit), `user-ns/op`, `sys-ns/op` and `peak-B`. Warm-up runs and failed runs are left out.

Where the programs printed result lines themselves, those lines are written in place of
the process times, as they were read, with the parameters of their combination added to
the name.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the text.

<a id="Lines.impl.fromGoogleBenchmark"></a>

### Associated function `fromGoogleBenchmark`

```silk
pub effect fn fromGoogleBenchmark(text: string) -> String
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns what Google Benchmark printed in `text`, its console table, as result lines: one
line for each row, with the row's iterations, its `Time` column as `ns/op` and its `CPU`
column as `cpu-ns/op`. A row `BM_Parse/64  98.1 ns  98.0 ns  7000000` becomes
`BenchmarkBM_Parse/64 7000000 98.1 ns/op 98 cpu-ns/op`.

#### Details
A line that is not a row is left out, and so are the rows Google Benchmark adds for
repetitions, whose names end in `_mean`, `_median`, `_stddev` or `_cv`: the task computes
its own statistics. Counters after the iterations are left out.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the text.

<a id="Lines.impl.fromCriterion"></a>

### Associated function `fromCriterion`

```silk
pub effect fn fromCriterion(text: string) -> String
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns what a Rust benchmark printed in `text` as result lines with 1 iteration and the
unit `ns/op`. Two shapes are read: Criterion's `name  time:   [low estimate high]`, of
which the estimate in the middle is taken, and the `test name ... bench: 1,240 ns/iter
(+/- 12)` of the built-in harness and of Criterion's `--output-format bencher`.

#### Details
Criterion writes a long name on a line of its own, before the line with `time:`; that
name is used. Every other line is left out. A space in a name becomes `_`.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the text.
